newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares end up but seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares end up but seen rangebound.

text.p: Slovenian shares edged higher on Friday but traders said the market lacked the impetus to break out of a narrow trading range in the coming week.
The blue chip SBI index firmed 0.96 points to 1,323.33 on turnover of 46.1 million tolars, down from 65.1 million.
Overall six shares rose, ten fell, two were unchanged and ten were untraded.
"Until parliament ratifies the association accord with the European Union no fresh money will flow in," a trader said.
Parliament is expected to take a vote on the issue in the next two weeks.
Bank UBK was the top gainer in the wake of Thursday's announcement that rival SBK was buying a 51 percent UBK stake. UBK shares jumped 9.21 percent to 6,880 tolars on only three contracts.
Traders said UBK could rally towards 8,000 tolars as the link-up was expected to ease the bank's liquidity problems.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded stock with 146 contracts. It slipped 0.14 percent to 49,100 tolars.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, down 11.41 percent to 13,200 on volume of 480 shares. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-12-58439
